definitions.explanation: a difficult situation from which escape seems impossible

examples.japanese: {窮地|きゅうち}に{陥|おちい}った。
{窮地|きゅうち}を{脱|だっ}する{方法|ほうほう}を{探|さが}している。
examples.english: I'm looking for a way to escape this predicament.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{何度|なんど}も{窮地|きゅうち}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えてきた。
examples.english: He has overcome many dire situations.

notes:
A formal word for a desperate situation from which escape seems very difficult.

FORMS:
{窮|きゅう} (cornered, exhausted) + {地|ち} (ground, position)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {窮地|きゅうち}に{陥|おちい}る: to fall into a predicament
- {窮地|きゅうち}に{立|た}たされる: to be placed in a tight spot
- {窮地|きゅうち}を{脱|だっ}する: to escape a predicament
- {窮地|きゅうち}に{追|お}い{込|こ}む: to drive someone into a corner
- {窮地|きゅうち}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}える: to overcome a dire situation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ピンチ: pinch, tight spot (casual, loanword)
- {苦境|くきょう}: difficult circumstances (slightly less severe)
- {危機|きき}: crisis (focuses on danger)
- {窮地|きゅうち} is more literary and dramatic than ピンチ.
